title: Probe Choreography and Ops Lab Notes
summary: Working notes for a lightweight probe choreography approach: how probes, tracing anchors, and dashboard tiles should be orchestrated for low-cost, high-signal observability of inference paths.
body:
Context and goal:
- Very practical ops-lab doc: small, pluggable probes + trace anchors + panel choreography to catch regressions early without exploding costs. Target: SREs + runtime and model-onboarding engineers.

Guiding principles (short):
- Signal-first: prefer a few high-quality probes over many noisy ones.
- Budget-aware sampling: fixed trace budget per minute per cluster, adaptive to burstiness.
- Probes live close to the user-facing edges (router, model-router, kv service).
- Dashboards should be tiled by symptom (latency, error, cold-cache) not by infra layer.

Probe types and placement (ops-lab flavors):
- Synthetic prefix probe (every 30s by region): validates warm-path for top-20 customer prefixes. Fires short request that exercises kv-cache, prefix fetch, model variant routing.
- Tail-latency microprobe (sampled 1/1000): long prompt to expose token-path worst cases. Attach full trace.
- KV-warmth sampler (frequency 1/60): checks cache hit rates and eviction churn for tenant cohorts.
- Canary output-quality probe (per rollout): runs eval prompts and captures embeddings + score.

Trace anchoring plan (unique ops-lab terms):
- Session ribbon: group microcalls in a single session id so traces across model-router, kv, and device can be stitched (use header X-RW-Session).
- Anchor spans: router.receive -> router.route -> model.call -> kv.get -> model.return. Keep anchors small and stable.
- Sampling budget: default 30 traces/min/region (adjustable); severity-weighted sampling for high-error paths.

Metric definitions (short, canonical):
- infra/latency/request_p95_ms: p95 of end-to-end request latency including network. Alert threshold: > 600ms for hosted API baseline.
- infra/latency/token_infer_p99_ms: p99 per-token generation time measured at runtime.
- kv/cache_hit_rate_tenant: hit rate for tenant namespace window=5m. Low threshold: < 0.6 triggers kv-warmth probe.
- routing/fallback_ratio: fraction of requests that used fallback model variant in last 5m. Soft alert: > 0.02.
- probe/synthetic_success_rate: percent success of synthetic probes by region. Use for canary health gating.

Dashboard choreography and tile rules:
- Tile 1: Global health lane — synthetic_success_rate, error_rate_5m, fallback_ratio. Minimal panels, critical.
- Tile 2: Latency ribbon — request_p50/p95/p99, token_infer_p95, grouped by model-family.
- Tile 3: KV warmth — cache_hit_rate_tenant heatmap, eviction_rate, top-20 cold tenants.
- Tile 4: Trace anchors — session ribbon trace count, top slow spans, sampled error traces (link to trace explorer).
- Ownership: each tile has an owner + backup (owner email alias placeholder). Ownership must be declared before rollout.

Investigation quickcards (operator-friendly):
- If request_p95 spikes: check synthetic_success_rate (tile 1) -> open sample traces in trace explorer -> look at session ribbon for KV waits -> check kv/cache_hit_rate_tenant for spikes.
- If tail token latency high: open tail-latency microprobe traces -> inspect model-call span for GPU stalls (blocked=1) and kernel-selection logs.
- If fallback_ratio increases: correlate rollout tags -> model-variant success logs -> trace anchors to see where routing failed.

Lab experiments and open questions (notes-to-self):
- Experiment: move synthetic prefix cadence from 30s -> 60s and compare signal/noise ratio; measure query-cost delta. JIRA-OPS-778 tracks.
- How granular should session ribbon IDs be for multi-call chat flows? tradeoff: stitchability vs privacy. Proposal: hash(user+short-timestamp) and rotate per 12h.
- Can we add severity-weighted sampling that biases toward traces with fallback or kv miss? Need infra support, filed GH PR linked above.
- Unresolved: optimal p99 gating thresholds for dedicated vs hosted; need historical baseline per model-family. Next step: extract baseline job (owner: Marco).

Onboarding checklist for a new model:
- Add model-family tags to token_infer metrics.
- Add at least one synthetic prefix probe exercising that model variant.
- Define baseline p95/p99 and register in metric-contract sheet.
- Add a lightweight dashboard tile under 'Latencies by model-family' and set owner.

Ops lab TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add session ribbon header to router SDK (Leah).
- [ ] Wire severity-weighted sampler (Jonas).
- [ ] Create panel templates for 'Tile 3: KV warmth' (Asha).
- [ ] Run cadence experiment 30s vs 60s for synthetic probes (track cost).

Snippets / quick queries (informal):
- count(trace) by span.name where span.name ~ "model.call" and duration > 500ms group by model.family
- avg(kv.cache_hit_rate_tenant) by tenant over 5m -> alert if < 0.6

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-1423: probe framework design notes (start here).
- JIRA-OPS-778: probe cadence experiment.
- GitHub PR: telemetry-probes/pull/89 (sampling prototype).

End notes: this is intentionally informal — the goal is to move fast with low-cost probes that give high debug value. If something grows noisy, prune immediately. We'll iterate panel designs in the ops-lab sessions next Wed.
